title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = -x^3
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = -x^3, state any symmetry the graph possesses, and specify the intervals over which the function is increasing or decreasing.
finalAnswer: \text{Symmetric about the origin; Decreasing on } (-\infty, \infty); \text{ Increasing nowhere}

steps.title: Test for Algebraic Symmetry
steps.explanation: Replacing x with -x negates the output, showing that f(x) = -x^3 is an odd function whose graph is symmetric about the origin.
steps.why: A function satisfying f(-x) = -f(x) on a symmetric domain has 180-degree rotational symmetry about the origin.

steps.title: Compare Outputs for x_1 < x_2
steps.explanation: Since the cubing function x^3 is strictly increasing on (-inf, inf), multiplying by -1 reverses the inequality so that -x_1^3 > -x_2^3 whenever x_1 < x_2.
steps.why: Multiplying a strictly increasing function by a negative constant produces a strictly decreasing function.

steps.title: State the Monotonicity Intervals
steps.explanation: The graph passes through (-1, 1), (0, 0), and (1, -1), falling continuously from Quadrant II into Quadrant IV across the entire real line (-inf, inf).
steps.why: Because f(x_1) > f(x_2) for all x_1 < x_2 in R, the function is decreasing on (-inf, inf).
